name: Yellowish sienna
lede: Yellowish sienna is ColorHub's name for Kabacha (樺茶), a traditional Japanese color glossed as "birch brown."

sections.title: Kabacha, a birch brown
sections.body:
Our library lists this color from the Wikipedia survey *Traditional colors of Japan*, under the romanized name Kabacha, written 樺茶 [1]. The kanji combine a word for birch with the general word for brown, and the library glosses the pair as "birch brown" [1]. The books consulted for this project give no further date or dyeing detail, so the naming story beyond that gloss is undocumented here [1].

In our library the nearest already-named color is [[sienna]], at a computed distance of 5.8, close enough that most eyes would call them the same warm reddish-brown [1]. By the numbers, though, yellowish sienna leans redder, at a hue angle of 42 degrees against sienna's 51, while plain sienna leans a touch more orange [1]. The hex given here, #B14A30, is a modern screen reading chosen to match the library's gloss, not a measurement of any pigment or dyed cloth, so treat it as approximate [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within range of this swatch in 427 of the 23,781 paintings we have, about 1.8 percent, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1400s, present in 67 of 945 paintings from that century, 3.95 times the rate expected from the century mix, and it appears in 68 of 721 Indian works, 5.25 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest dated appearance we have is a Tibetan votive card from the year 1000, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a true first sighting [2].

Inside a painting it most often sits as a midtone, in 68 percent of the paintings that carry it, with a shadow role in 17 percent [2]. Measured values are screen approximations of varnished, photographed canvases, not a pigment identification [2].
